items.text: A Brexit reversal is on the table 10 years on from the vote. Here’s what’s at stake
items.article: Britain voted to leave the European Union in 2016. U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham suggested this week that British voters could be given the chance to reverse Brexit, the country's highly contentious departure from the European Union a decade ago. Burnham, who became prime minister over the summer, told the BBC on Wednesday it was "possible" a referendum on rejoining the EU could be included in a future election manifesto. A U.K. general election is not currently expected before 2029. Prime ministers are able to trigger an early snap election with the backing of parliament, but Burnham — who replaced predecessor Keir Starmer without a public vote — has ruled out such a move. In his interview with the BBC, the prime minister said a referendum "wouldn't be the right thing to do right now," but added that the U.K. must "consider the options" for its relationship with the EU, arguing that "where we are isn't good enough." Asked whether an in-out referendum in a future election manifesto was a possibility, Burnham said: "yes, things are possible." During the previous general election — which saw Starmer lead the governing Labour party to a landslide victory and end 14 years of Conservative rule — Burnham was serving as Mayor of Manchester. As he prepared to challenge Starmer's leadership, Burnham pledged not to "re-run" arguments over Brexit.

Shivakumar, accompanied by several Cabinet colleagues, submitted a memorandum to the Chief Electoral Officer in Bengaluru and staged a protest outside the office. He alleged that large numbers of Form 7 applications were filed and later withdrawn in constituencies including Ballari, Vijayapura, Belagavi, Mysuru and Bidar, and claimed that pre-printed forms containing voter details were being distributed. Meanwhile, EC said it would initiate legal proceedings against those responsible for the bulk filing of Form 7 applications seeking deletion of voters during the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Karnataka. Kegs are stacked outside the pubs around the square. Restaurants are loading up on provisions. Tourists gravitate towards Eyre Square, once an open ground used by market traders outside Galway’s medieval town gate, now enveloped by the city and its centrepiece. Named after former mayor of Galway Edward Eyre, who donated the land to the city in 1710, the square is surrounded by historic and modern buildings. Recent additions contrast sharply with the late Georgian and Victorian buildings, many of which struggle to find a use in modern Galway as they stand either vacant or underused. items.text: Why You Should Avoid Overdoing It On Sugar When You're On Antibiotics
items.article: A new study suggests eating sugary foods on antibiotics might be amplifying damage done to the gut. Antibiotics are some of the most prescribed drugs around the world – and while they’re handy for fighting a whole host of bacterial infections, anyone who’s been on them will know they can also wreak havoc on gut health . On a very simple level, the medication targets bacteria in the body to kill off the bad stuff – unfortunately it can also get rid of the good stuff, too. “The extent to which antibiotics affect the gut depends on several factors,” Dr Megan Rossi, a gut health scientist at King’s College London, previously told HuffPost UK, suggesting that the type of antibiotic matters (broad-spectrum ones, for example, affect a wider range of bacteria in the gut), as does the dose (prolonged or repeated courses can have a greater cumulative impact). And if you eat sugar-filled snacks while you’re taking them, it may well worsen the harm caused to the bacteria in the gut, a new study suggests. The microbiome can typically resist a buildup of nasty pathogens when it’s functioning normally, but antibiotics can reduce the natural species diversity in the gut and make it more vulnerable to disease. Researchers tracked every food item in 9,419 meals eaten by 173 hospitalised cancer patients and then measured their gut microbiome changes.

items.text: Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt says AI beat him at the thing he did best
items.article: The former Google CEO said today's AI coding tools surpass his skills and free up programmers to be the architects, not the ones who build the house. The former Google CEO said AI has beaten him at the thing he was once best at. Eric Schmidt, now 71, told Blackstone's "Inside Blackstone" podcast that he was among the top programmers of his generation, but today's AI coding tools are writing the code he couldn't. "I was a very, very good programmer when I was 22, right? I was one of the best, according to myself. My field is over, right?" Schmidt told podcast host Christine Anderson. "I look at the code it writes now. I can't write that code. I couldn't when I was 22, right? So, I got beaten, right? Hard." Still, Schmidt tells young people to learn to code so they can give the most accurate orders to AI tools and be the brains of the design. "I had to build the house," Schmidt said in an analogy. "Now I can architect the house using the equivalent of Claude Code or OpenAI Codex or future products from Google, which they're working on, all of which allow me to say what I want and the code gets written." "The next generation of people like me will be the architects, and they'll be very, very smart and they know how to say, 'this is what I want,'" Schmidt added.

items.text: Nominated Five Times, Why Was Mahatma Gandhi Never Awarded The Nobel Peace Prize?
items.article: As India marks Gandhi Jayanti, a look back at the Nobel Committee's decisions that kept the world's most famous advocate of non-violence from its Peace Prize. Mahatma Gandhi became one of the strongest symbols of non-violence in the 20th century, with his philosophy of satyagraha shaping India’s freedom struggle and leaving an influence far beyond the country. Yet the Nobel Peace Prize never came his way. It wasn’t for lack of consideration. Gandhi was nominated for the Nobel Peace Prize five times — in 1937, 1938, 1939, 1947 and 1948 — and made the Norwegian Nobel Committee’s shortlist on multiple occasions. His omission was publicly regretted by later members of the Nobel Committee. In 1989, when the Dalai Lama received the Nobel Peace Prize, the committee chairman said the award was “in part a tribute to the memory of Mahatma Gandhi". What Happened When Gandhi Was First Nominated? Gandhi was first nominated in 1937 by Ole Colbjørnsen, a Labour Party member of the Norwegian Parliament. He was among 13 candidates shortlisted for the Nobel Peace Prize that year. By then, Gandhi had long established non-violence as a central principle of his political struggle. He had developed satyagraha , or “truth force", while campaigning for Indians in South Africa and later used non-violent resistance against British rule in India.

items.article: Most of the betting industry is urging the chancellor not to double slot machine duty to raise up to £460m more a year Gambling industry kingpins are fuming about reports that the chancellor, John Healey, is considering increasing taxes on high-street slot machines in his first budget. The influential Social Market Foundation thinktank, the most vocal advocate for a rise in machine games duty (MGD), from 20% to 40%, thinks the measure could raise between £275m and £460m annually , on top of the roughly £610m collected last year. Its proposal is likely to meet with sympathy from Andy Burnham, a vocal and repeated critic of slot machines , who has already moved to tighten licensing laws so that gambling firms find it harder to open up new shops. The billionaire owner of Betfred, Fred Done, is among industry bosses who say such a policy would force shop closures, cost jobs and ultimately fail in its objective, depriving the Treasury of taxes. But not every figure in the gambling world agrees. Stewart Kenny, the co-founder of Paddy Power who has become a critic of his erstwhile industry, accused Done of “scaremongering”.

items.article: Milk Bar founder Christina Tosi said she saw an opportunity in hiring women leaders — and turned it into a business advantage. Milk Bar founder Christina Tosi said the key to hiring a great team is learning to do the jobs yourself first. "For the longest time, I demanded of myself to work the job, whether that was human resources, or ops, or the delivery driver, or the pick-pack-ship person," Tosi said on Thursday's episode of the " Pretty Tough with Maria Sharapova " podcast. Whenever the company needed to create a new role, Tosi said she first wanted to understand what the job involved before hiring someone to do it. "What is it like to work this job? What are the highs and the lows? What kind of personality would it take?" she said. "And then, how do I find someone who can be better than me at it?" Beyond technical skills, Tosi said she looked for people she would want beside her, "celebrating the highs, and being in the trenches on the hard days and lows with." She added that she was focused on hiring women for leadership roles because of how difficult she had found it to gain opportunities herself.

But history offers a warning to Democrats, as polls in recent elections underestimated Republicans in key states. Control of the Senate could come down to just a handful of races where polls show razor-thin margins. Alaska , Iowa , Maine , Michigan , Ohio and Texas have emerged as the most competitive races where both parties are hopeful about their chances. Recent polling points to tight races in each of those states. But Republicans have outperformed polling averages in many of those same states over the past few elections. Polling errors are not necessarily repeated from cycle to cycle. But a similar pro-Republican polling error this cycle would not bode well for Democrats’ chances of flipping the Senate. It’s “impossible to know for sure” what the polling error could look like this year, Grant Davis Reeher, professor of political science at Syracuse University, told Newsweek. “There are some pretty big known unknowns in this election, which could throw off polls,” he said. “A primary one is turnout. Store closures this year have generally remained below the levels seen during recent retail downturns, but a growing number of stores are still shrinking their physical footprints in response to changing shopping habits. For shoppers, that means familiar stores may vanish from their local shopping centers this October and through the fall. The latest round of closures reflects a major shift in American retail. items.article: This port town serves as a welcoming base for an autumn trip to the Outer Hebrides For many people, Stornoway is a brief stop-off as they travel through its ferry port or airport en route to adventures in the Outer Hebrides. Canny visitors stay a little longer, soaking up the atmosphere of a town that is not just a tourist gateway, but the heart of a vibrant island community and an active fishing port. Although English is the dominant language here, Scottish Gaelic is still spoken. Walking along the attractive harbourfront, holidaymakers may notice that the town’s street signs are written in both languages. Stornoway is the largest town in the Outer Hebrides and capital of the island of Lewis . Indoor attractions include the lively An Lanntair arts centre, which hosts traditional music sessions and arts workshops; and Lews Castle Museum, whose collection includes six of the 12th-century Lewis Chessmen – chess pieces made from carved walrus ivory and whales’ teeth, which was featured in Harry Potter and the Philosopher’s Stone.
